Abstract:

Real-world dynamical systems evolve through complex nonlinear interactions under sparse and noisy observations, with largely unknown governing mechanisms. This work develops a unified data-driven framework for modeling real-world dynamics, with emphasis on uncertainty-aware forecasting and objective index construction. In this thesis, socio-economic indicators are modeled as continuous-time latent processes using a hybrid recurrent encoder and Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODEs), enabling accurate representation of heterogeneous temporal dynamics, interpolation, and long-horizon forecasting. In order to incorporate stochasticity, the framework is extended to variational Neural Stochastic Differential Equations (Neural SDEs), capturing both long-term trends and short-term fluctuations while providing calibrated uncertainty estimates and distinguishing region-specific volatility patterns. Further, an interval-based learning approach is introduced through Interval Neural Network (INN) formulations, enabling bounded predictions and systematic uncertainty quantification. Additionally, data-driven composite indices based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA) are introduced, using primary data collected from KBK districts of Odisha and secondary data from open sources. The clustering of these indices reveals persistent regional disparities and recent reversals in socio-economic trends. Overall, the proposed methodologies advance interpretable, uncertainty-aware machine learning for robust socio-economic modeling and policy design.
